ranking_basis: fit to constrained one-online-evaluator roadmap, essential baselines and security-relevant comparisons; not a speed ranking

papers.title: Dash: Accelerating Distributed Private Convolutional Neural Network Inference with Arithmetic Garbled Circuits
papers.source_summary: Arithmetic garbling and LabelTensors provide the foundation for offline preparation and local encoded public-weight evaluation.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement affine-label arithmetic, constant multiplication with the required algebraic preconditions, projections and tensorized evaluation. Preserve the original circuit functionality before adapting to transformers.
papers.benchmark_contract: Original CNN/model workloads first; then matched public linear operators and a fixed-point decoder region. Report label lanes, storage and all setup.
papers.security_boundary: Do not inherit malicious security by importing kernels: the paper discusses additional integrity mechanisms and trusted-hardware or cryptographic configurations.
papers.prior_evidence: Prior single-server, model-aware and tenx archives contain adaptations, not a reproduced Dash release.

papers.title: ReDASH: Fast and efficient Scaling in Arithmetic Garbled Circuits for Secure Outsourced Inference
papers.source_summary: ReDASH generalizes residue-number-system scaling and uses ScaleQuant+ to reduce encoded-inference overhead.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement signed base extension, the published scaling gadget and its quantization policy as separately versioned components. Expose exact and approximate semantics explicitly.
papers.benchmark_contract: Exhaustive small CRT domains, signed boundary fixtures, reference CNN comparison and identical decoder-region rescaling.
papers.security_boundary: Preserve the specified sign/scaling assumptions. Modular inversion is not ordinary fixed-point division; per-residue ReLU is not global integer ReLU.
papers.prior_evidence: Only researched previously; earlier CRT kernels did not implement full ReDASH scaling.

papers.title: Garbling Gadgets for Boolean and Arithmetic Circuits
papers.source_summary: Arithmetic garbling provides free additions and specialized gadgets, with a stated symmetric-primitive security model.
papers.proposed_implementation: Create a reviewed arithmetic-label core with modulus-specific offsets, permitted constant operations, projection and mixed-modulus gadgets. Keep offsets opaque.
papers.benchmark_contract: Published gadget truth tables and byte formulas, negative constant/modulus cases, exhaustive finite-domain differential tests.
papers.security_boundary: Functionality alone does not validate affine-label correlations or an arbitrary hash replacement. Reject unsupported non-unit constants or lower them through justified gadgets.
papers.prior_evidence: Affine-label arithmetic exists in archived references; no proof-equivalent native port has been established.

papers.title: Two Halves Make a Whole: Reducing Data Transfer in Garbled Circuits using Half Gates
papers.source_summary: Half-gates reduce AND-gate communication while remaining compatible with free XOR.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement Boolean label ownership, free XOR and half-gates using a precisely documented reviewed hash instantiation. Batch native cryptographic operations and expose circuit I/O conversions.
papers.benchmark_contract: All input truth assignments, independent original-artifact differential cases, two-ciphertext accounting and native AES/SIMD benchmarks.
papers.security_boundary: Free-XOR-compatible correlation assumptions, domain separation and circuit freshness are mandatory. Malicious garbler defenses are a separate construction.
papers.prior_evidence: Python SHA-based half-gates in tenx references are adaptations; not a native audited implementation.

papers.title: Garbled Circuit Lookup Tables with Logarithmic Number of Ciphertexts
papers.source_summary: The lookup construction reduces the number of security-parameter-sized ciphertexts; total communication retains a table-data term.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce the original lookup construction, not its headline complexity. Provide Boolean input/output contracts and explicit arithmetic conversion edges.
papers.benchmark_contract: Matched 8/12/16-bit tables versus flat, Boolean and weighted-path variants. Include the table-data term and both conversion directions.
papers.security_boundary: Do not translate logarithmic ciphertext count into logarithmic total bytes or claim our flat-table improvements beat this unimplemented baseline.
papers.prior_evidence: Analytical formulas only in previous work; no original or PLLM logrow execution.

papers.title: Duty-Free Bits: Projectivizing Garbling Schemes
papers.source_summary: This work studies projective conversion from Yao-style bit labels into affine encodings and related vector-OLE applications.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement only conversions justified by the acquired full specification. Represent input/output label families, field, security assumptions and direction as types.
papers.benchmark_contract: Published conversion test vectors and complete Boolean-to-arithmetic regions; compare widths and include the reverse path only if separately implemented.
papers.security_boundary: The title does not grant free bidirectional conversion or a safe interface from freely editable masked scalars.
papers.prior_evidence: Primary abstract consulted; full construction acquisition and review are blocking tasks.

papers.title: Slalom: Fast, Verifiable and Private Execution of Neural Networks in Trusted Hardware
papers.source_summary: Slalom outsources masked linear work and uses local verification within a trusted execution partition.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce the original blinding and verification boundary. Register PLLM trusted-client/dealer adaptation separately; port modular kernels and verification state without changing the numerical graph silently.
papers.benchmark_contract: Original representative layers; archived PLLM partition; same clear integer graph, unmasked remote partition and optimized native model as separate baselines.
papers.security_boundary: A trusted client is not a reproduced TEE deployment. Static non-collusion, integrity and later compromise require distinct claims.
papers.prior_evidence: Original PLLM manuscript reports nine Qwen runs; this archive is not a fresh reproduction of Slalom.

papers.title: Slalom at the Carnival: Privacy-preserving Inference with Masks from Public Knowledge
papers.source_summary: Carnival uses subset-sum-based masks to accelerate preprocessing for linear outsourcing.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement the exact published parameterized variant in an isolated comparison backend. Reproduce the reported Maverick attack before eligibility review.
papers.benchmark_contract: Preparation time, traffic, distribution tests and the specific published attack, with the attacked variant and assumptions identified.
papers.security_boundary: Maverick reports a privacy flaw for a Carnival instantiation. This is an attack-reproduction target, not an approved default or a blanket rejection of every variant.
papers.prior_evidence: Prior discussion identified this attack; no claim that our fresh full-ring masks instantiate Carnival.

papers.title: HyCC: Compilation of Hybrid Protocols for Practical Secure Computation
papers.source_summary: HyCC compiles high-level programs into hybrid secure-computation protocols.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce a fixed published hybrid-selection benchmark. Separate its original frontend and backend assumptions from PLLM region planning, protected-state effects and generative workloads.
papers.benchmark_contract: Best uniform backend versus legal regional selection; include conversion, peak memory and preparation rather than only kernel time.
papers.security_boundary: A cost optimizer cannot trade away a privacy contract or numeric semantics. Type-correct composition is not an automatic security theorem.
papers.prior_evidence: Prior architecture cites HyCC; original artifact not run. Canonical DOI verified via author-source metadata; full text must be locked.

papers.title: Oblivious decision program evaluation
papers.source_summary: Oblivious decision-program protocols evaluate protected decision structures using OT-based reductions.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce the original actor roles first. Then separately specify a model-aware garbler/offline-dealer adaptation for encoded nonlinear paths, including all input label delivery.
papers.benchmark_contract: Fixed public depths, original decision-program fixtures, path access observables and arithmetic I/O conversion costs.
papers.security_boundary: Role reversal and arithmetic output are adaptations. Fixed path length alone does not prove that node identities or graph topology are hidden.
papers.prior_evidence: Weighted transducer archive uses related ideas but is not a reproduction of this protocol.

papers.title: Factored Edge-Valued Binary Decision Diagrams
papers.source_summary: Factored edge-valued diagrams share subfunctions through additive and multiplicative edge normalization.
papers.proposed_implementation: Port public EVBDD/FEVBDD compilation, canonical residual normalization and variable-order search to Rust. Keep encrypted traversal as a separate experimental method.
papers.benchmark_contract: Exhaustive fixed integer LUT equivalence, graph hashes, node counts and compile-memory measurements; then separately benchmark protected execution.
papers.security_boundary: This is function compression, not a privacy protocol. No security claim follows from a smaller public graph.
papers.prior_evidence: Prior tenx archive contains exact public diagram experiments and a custom encrypted extension.

papers.title: Piranha: A GPU Platform for Secure Computation
papers.source_summary: Piranha separates device, protocol and application layers for GPU-accelerated secret-sharing computation.
papers.proposed_implementation: Wrap original GPU kernels through a narrow native interface before selective Rust/CUDA ports. Preserve protocol party counts and numeric domains in comparisons.
papers.benchmark_contract: Integer-kernel parity and matching original protocol workloads; device execution and transfer time, all workers and GPU allocation counted.
papers.security_boundary: Kernel reuse does not turn a multi-online-worker protocol into the preferred single-evaluator topology.
papers.prior_evidence: Previous CPU limb/packing experiments are not a GPU Piranha reproduction.

papers.title: SIGMA: Secure GPT Inference with Function Secret Sharing
papers.source_summary: SIGMA provides FSS-based secure transformer operations and GPU-backed inference with preprocessing.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce the original FSS helpers and complete reference workload. Register softmax, activation, normalization and truncation independently with exact phase contracts.
papers.benchmark_contract: Original model/token accounting first; sustained autoregressive decode is a separate workload, not inferred from one forward-pass time.
papers.security_boundary: Two online parties and the dealer model must remain explicit. No implicit substitution into the one-evaluator default.
papers.prior_evidence: Resident-share and spectral archives are different constructions, not SIGMA reproductions.

papers.title: FuseFSS: Efficient Secure LLM Inference with Function Secret Sharing
papers.source_summary: FuseFSS targets fusion and efficiency of secure nonlinear/helper operations in FSS-based LLM inference.
papers.proposed_implementation: Acquire and pin the full source and artifact; port complete fused helpers with their offline key generation, remaining secure multiplication and rescaling.
papers.benchmark_contract: Matched SIGMA functions, bit widths, hardware and token workloads; count every online dependency and fresh key byte.
papers.security_boundary: A fused key lookup does not make subsequent private polynomial evaluation free. Public model support does not eliminate the second online role.
papers.prior_evidence: Prior reference fused-polynomial experiments are alternative methods, not a FuseFSS implementation.

papers.title: Efficient Pseudorandom Correlation Generators over Z/p^k Z
papers.source_summary: Galois-ring constructions extend pseudorandom correlation generation to integer rings, including multiplication-related correlations.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement reviewed parameter sets and the actual requested correlation schema. Expose seed setup, expansion time, memory and transcript requirements; do not substitute ordinary PRG seeds.
papers.benchmark_contract: Correct correlation identities, original artifact outputs, communication versus expansion compute, and current attack-aware parameter checks.
papers.security_boundary: PCGs do not automatically compress arbitrary garbled tables or spectral coefficients. Small toy parameters are not deployment security parameters.
papers.prior_evidence: Earlier Galois-ring checks were algebra only, not a PCG implementation.

papers.title: Practical Secure Delegated Linear Algebra with Trapdoored Matrices
papers.source_summary: This work uses trapdoored pseudorandom matrices for efficient delegated linear algebra under an LPN-based approach.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement the paper-specific matrix/trapdoor generation and delegation protocol before attempting a setup adaptation. State who knows each operand and each trapdoor.
papers.benchmark_contract: Original linear workloads, malicious-result handling where specified, full client/offline work and public-model-adaptation comparison.
papers.security_boundary: Public low-rank masks leak nullspace projections. This construction must not be approximated by an unproven structured mask.
papers.prior_evidence: Identified as a lead previously; not executed in the supplied archives.

papers.title: Curl: Private LLMs through Wavelet-Encoded Look-Up Tables
papers.source_summary: Curl uses wavelet-encoded lookup tables for private nonlinear operations and discusses probabilistic truncation security.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce original lookup construction, encoding, scale and truncation behavior. Treat a wavelet approximation imported into garbling as a separate numerical/protocol adaptation.
papers.benchmark_contract: Log/reciprocal/activation functions at matched numeric accuracy, preprocessing and helper rounds, then original language-model fixtures.
papers.security_boundary: A stand-alone truncation argument does not imply universal composability. Sparse transform coefficients do not make private access free.
papers.prior_evidence: Prior report cited Curl; no Curl protocol was reproduced.

papers.title: Compact: Approximating Complex Activation Functions for Secure Computation
papers.source_summary: Compact builds input-density-aware piecewise polynomial approximations for complex activations.
papers.proposed_implementation: Implement its fitting objective and published approximation profile separately from protected evaluation. Freeze coefficient/interval hashes and add explicit tail policy.
papers.benchmark_contract: Approximation envelopes and full-checkpoint quality, not scalar error alone; protected evaluator includes interval selection and all truncation.
papers.security_boundary: Calibration is not a proof of a worst-case range. Model quality and exact agreement with the chosen approximation are distinct.
papers.prior_evidence: Our Fourier/boundary-matched fits are distinct hypotheses, not Compact reproductions.

papers.title: Private and Verifiable Outsourcing of Open-Weight LLM Inference
papers.source_summary: The abstract describes private and verifiable open-weight inference with two malicious, non-colluding servers and model-owner-published information.
papers.proposed_implementation: Acquire the complete protocol and original artifact first. Create a faithful isolated adapter with a documented client, model-owner, server and proof boundary.
papers.benchmark_contract: Original workload versus true autoregressive decoding, setup/model-owner cost, online server multiplicity and complete verification costs.
papers.security_boundary: Abstract claims alone do not specify a reproducible protocol or near-native sustained TPS. This remains source-acquisition-gated.
papers.prior_evidence: Only abstract-level comparison exists in the supplied work.

papers.title: Oblivious Ciphertext Compression via Linear Codes
papers.source_summary: This work develops oblivious ciphertext compression using linear codes and syndrome decoding.
papers.proposed_implementation: Reproduce the exact source construction and its decoding-side-information assumptions. Bind codecs to representations and valid domains; compare the PLLM syndrome design as an adaptation.
papers.benchmark_contract: Original correctness domain, payload and encoder/decoder cost; public-bound packing and uncompressed matched controls; explicit out-of-domain collision cases.
papers.security_boundary: Lossless compression is conditional on its domain and side information. Successful decode is not proof of correct inference, and adaptive retries can leak.
papers.prior_evidence: Network archives contain a custom bounded-overflow codec, not this paper's implementation.
